correctness.rationale: The section vertices coincide with transverse edge crossings; every possible vertex great-circle wall has two positive and two negative neighboring normal projections because of two radial neighbor pairs. Thus edge crossing count cannot change through a wall. In exact Q(sqrt5) arithmetic all 30 pairings, 32 supporting facets, 60 edges and equal radius phi are verified using the bundled checker, run to completion. Haar integral geometry gives each of the 60 edges crossing probability 1/5 because the central angle is pi/5; expectation 12 determines the universal generic count. Degenerate planes excluded explicitly.

value.rationale: The exact complete central-section polygon-type classification of a classical non-zonohedral Archimedean polyhedron is natural and structurally surprising. Its polygon sides remain 12 for every generic plane despite two different facet types. The reusable radial-neighbor-pair lemma and Crofton shortcut explain the invariant without an orientation census, rather than merely computing one sample or a small numerical refinement.
